chunks: My father (peace be upon him) narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'If you shun the great sins which you are forbidden,' he said: 'One who abstains from those sins for which Allah has promised Hell, if he is a believer, Allah will forgive his sins.'
ai.seo_question: How does abstaining from major sins lead to the forgiveness of minor sins according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the conditionality of divine forgiveness, linking the expiation of minor sins directly to the avoidance of major transgressions. This interpretation underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the hierarchy of sins, where the preservation of core faith through avoiding major sins serves as the mechanism for cleansing lesser faults, reinforcing the concept of *kaffarat al-sayyi'at* (expiation of sins) as a dynamic spiritual process rather than a static guarantee.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 2.  Imam Ridha (a.s.) says regarding the verse ‘If you shun the great sins which you are forbidden, We will do away with your small, “One who abstains from those sins for which Allah has promised Hell, Allah will forgive his (lesser) sins.”
